[[Tennis]] was one of the 28 sports that was held at the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] in [[Sydney]], [[Australia]]. The competition which was held from 19-28 September at the [[NSW Tennis Centre]], saw four gold medals being contested with them being in the singles and doubles of both sexes.

The format at the 2000 Olympics was a [[Single-elimination tournament|single-elimination]] tournament with the men's and women's singles being 64 players. They competed in six rounds of competition in the singles and five rounds in the doubles (sizes of 32). The format consisted of three set matches with five set matches being only played in the men's singles and doubles final. 

The [[United States at the 2000 Summer Olympics|United States]] finished on top of the medal table with two gold medals as [[Venus Williams]] won both the [[Tennis at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's singles|women's singles]] and [[Tennis at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Women's doubles|doubles]] with [[Serena Williams]]. In the men's events, [[Yevgeny Kafelnikov]] from [[Russia at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Russia]] secured the [[Tennis at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's singles|men's singles]] title while [[Canada at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Canadian]] pair, [[Sébastien Lareau]] and [[Daniel Nestor]] took the [[Tennis at the 2000 Summer Olympics – Men's doubles|men's doubles]].
